# ds-completion with its own decoder of the Engram table (README step 168), built against the pinned llama.cpp
# (b72050d03) and against upstream master e626db7ca (2026-11-20): the gates and the held-out prompts.
# Commit 9a57d22 + step 168's change (the commit that adds this file); sclk 6 on the four GPUs; 2026-11-21.
# The machine had been restarted: the model files were read through first (488 GB in the page cache).
# Three builds: "old" = 9a57d22 against the pin (bin/, bin-hip/ as built before the change);
#               "pin" = the change against the pin (make && make HIP=1);
#               "trunk" = the change against upstream (make FORK=<upstream> BIN=bin-trunk && make HIP=1 FORK=<upstream> BIN=bin-trunk-hip;
#                         upstream built with QUICKSTART's two cmake lines; every program of `make` and `make HIP=1` built).
#
# 1. The gates, per build (G=data/golden/hello-fp32, 5 steps; F8=dense-fp8.gguf):
#      <bin>/ds-test -m $M -g $G                       and  ... --e2e cpu.f32     (the CPU path, ggml graphs)
#      <bin-hip>/ds-test -m $M -g $G --runtime $F8     and  ... --e2e rt.f32      (the GPU runtime)
#    The --e2e files (the logits of the 5 steps, 2,585,600 bytes) compared with cmp; the per-layer tables row by row,
#    the last column (ms) left out.
